title: Free-text 'why did I take this trade' entry notes
description: Ch. 59 Section A of Elder's Trade Journal asks why the trader decided to take this trade -- a free-text note at entry time. No field for this exists anywhere in this app today (PositionIn has no notes field).

checklist.step: Add a nullable free-text `entry_notes` field to PositionIn/PositionOut/PositionORM.
Carry `entry_notes` through to ClosedTradeORM/ClosedTradeOut when a position closes.
Unit/integration tests for a position created with and without notes, and that notes carry through correctly to the closed trade row on close.

decisions.decision: On POST /api/portfolio/positions merging into an existing same-ticker position, an incoming `entry_notes` is appended to the existing note (joined by a blank line, `\n\n`) rather than overwriting it or being silently dropped. A merge with no incoming note leaves the existing note untouched.
decisions.rationale: Elder's Section A note captures 'why did I take this trade' at entry time; when a second buy merges into the same position, both original reasons are still relevant and neither should be lost. Overwrite would silently discard the first buy's rationale; ignoring the new note on merge would silently discard the second. Appending (mirroring the plain-text, human-readable nature of this field, unlike the numeric quantity/avg_cost_basis merge which needs one blended number) preserves both without inventing a structured multi-note schema this MVP doesn't otherwise need.

decisions.decision: `entry_notes` is carried on `app.portfolio.pricing.EnrichedPosition` as its own field (populated from `PositionORM.entry_notes` in `enrich_positions_with_price`) rather than being added to the shared `app.portfolio.models.Position` domain model that `EnrichedPosition.position` wraps.
decisions.rationale: `Position` is reused by `app.portfolio.risk`/`app.portfolio.exits`, which have no use for a free-text note, and its serialization shape is pinned exactly to the `GET /api/portfolio` JSON example in `docs/architecture/API.md` via `tests/unit/test_portfolio_models.py`'s byte-for-byte round-trip test. Adding an unused field there would mean either updating that pinned example/test for a field two of its three consumers never touch, or accepting drift. Keeping `entry_notes` alongside `daily_ohlcv` on `EnrichedPosition` (which already exists precisely to carry extra per-position context past `Position` itself) avoids both, at the cost of one extra dataclass field GET /api/portfolio's handler reads directly.

comments.summary: entry_notes has no field_validator to strip whitespace or normalize an empty string to null, unlike PositionIn.ticker's own strip-and-reject-blank validator. An explicit entry_notes: "" is stored/returned as "" rather than null, and a whitespace-only note is truthy so it would still get appended on a merge. Low severity, non-blocking -- filed as backend-trade-journal-entry-notes-followups.

review.notes: Full review: pytest --cov=app (949 passed, 99.94% coverage, no regression), ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc all clean, code-review skill (effort=high) found no correctness bugs. Verified the two decisions recorded above actually hold: (1) adding entry_notes to Position would break tests/unit/test_portfolio_models.py's exact-dict equality against the docs/architecture/API.md example (Position has no model_config excluding None fields from model_dump(mode="json")), and app.portfolio.risk/exits both consume Position directly with no use for entry_notes -- placement on EnrichedPosition is correct; (2) the merge-append behavior is tested for all four combinations (no-note create, note+no-incoming keeps existing, note+note appends blank-line-separated with neither note dropped, no-existing+incoming sets it) in tests/integration/test_portfolio_positions.py. backend/openapi.json and frontend/src/api/types.ts regenerated locally and confirmed byte-identical to the committed snapshot. Migration a9adc10fa37c verified as the single head with a correct up/down pair. No UI surface touched (only generated types.ts) -- browser walkthrough and e2e suite genuinely not applicable, explicitly skipped.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran pytest --cov=app: 949 passed, 99.94% coverage, matches review claim exactly. Also skimmed the full diff (backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py, schemas.py, db/models.py, portfolio/pricing.py, migration a9adc10fa37c, API.md, followups task) -- consistent with recorded decisions, no dropped concerns.
